answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-compute staking: before an agent can earn fees, it must lock a hardware-bound stake recorded as an onyx token and burn a little work each epoch. Without the stake, identities are hollow, costing nothing to mass-spawn. A real attacker pays twice, locked capital per identity plus continuous compute, while a saffron-tinted public ledger links each stake to one attestation chain so duplicate agents get slashed.
